title: Social Influence of Chronic Pelvic Pain in Endometriosis: Partnership Interaction
summary:
Endometriosis is a common chronic gynecological disease in which tissue similar to the endometrium grows outside the uterus and pain is the main symptom. 
Research has shown that social learning processes influence pain processing. However, the types of social interaction and coping strategies that could help women with chronic abdominal pain due to endometriosis have not yet been clarified. The aim of the research project is therefore to gain more information about social factors in chronic abdominal pain and to investigate a minimal couple intervention that can be easily integrated into everyday life.
The role of the hormones oxytocin and cortisol will also be investigated (for this purpose, daily profiles of the hormones from saliva samples will be analyzed repeatedly), as these two hormones have been shown to be associated with relationship variables and pain in past studies.

There will be two survey phases in our study, each lasting 7 days. The survey phases will take place during the menstrual periods of the endometriosis sufferers in consecutive months. Accordingly, there will be a break of approx. 2-4 weeks between the two phases.

The timing of the survey as well as the end of the survey is based on the participant's menses and is therefore determined individually. The survey is expected to be completed approximately 3-4 months after the initial contact.  The planned end of the entire study is 06/2027.

interventions.name: 7 days EMA (6x digital mini questionnaires and parallel saliva sampling) - 3 weeks break - 7 days EMA + intervention (3x 10-minute attention control on positive relationship aspects)
7 days EMA + intervention- 3 weeks break - 7 days EMA

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Subjects with the ability to follow study instructions and likely to attend and complete all required visits 
• Written informed consent of the participant 
• Willingness of the participant to receive SMS to their own smartphones and fill out short questionnaires using the provided link
• Being committed to an ongoing romantic relationship and living as a couple for at least 6 months 
• Subjects are able to speak, write and understand the German language sufficiently well (at the investigators discretion) to complete all required study procedures 

Additional inclusion criteria for patients: 
• Impairment due to chronic pelvic pain due to endometriosis 
• Age 18 – 45
• Existence of menstruation and regular cycle
Exclusion criteria:
Patients suffering from other (chronic) pain conditions, cancer, neurological, gynecologi-cal diseases, psychosis or psychoactive medication, or substance use disorders, or current pregnancy will be excluded from participation.

For all participants (including partners): 
• Withdrawal of participant consent (defined as a study participant who explicitly takes back his or her consent) is possible at all times during the study.
